title: Why no trousers, makeup or jewellery?
dek: Understanding the ministry's teaching on holiness: what the standard is, the passages behind it, where it is an application rather than a command — and why a changed heart, not a changed wardrobe, is what the Bible measures.
body:
The Ministry of Repentance and Holiness is built around a simple but serious message: **repent, live in holiness, walk in righteousness, and prepare for the return of Jesus Christ.**

The ministry teaches that Christianity is not only about believing in Jesus. It is also about the way a believer lives after turning to God. Its own description of itself is a call to the Church and to humanity to return to repentance, holiness and obedience to the Word of God in preparation for the coming of Christ.

That is why it places strong emphasis on how believers behave, speak, dress and conduct themselves.

For someone meeting these teachings for the first time, one question comes up more than any other: **why don't women in the ministry wear trousers, makeup or jewellery?**

To understand the answer, you have to start with what the ministry means by **holiness and separation from the world** — not with the clothing.

## What does the ministry mean by holiness?

For the Ministry of Repentance and Holiness, holiness means setting one's life apart for God.

The ministry teaches that when a person truly repents, their life should begin to change. Their choices, their behaviour and their appearance should reflect a commitment to God rather than the values and fashions of the world.

That is connected to Paul's words:

> Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind.
> — Romans 12:2, NIV

The ministry takes the instruction seriously. The question is not *"is everyone else doing it?"* but *"does this way of living agree with the life God wants for His people?"*

This understanding of holiness is also bound up with the ministry's emphasis on preparing believers for the return of Christ. What the word means, and what it does not, is set out in [what "without holiness no man shall see the Lord" means](/articles/what-does-without-holiness-no-man-shall-see-the-lord-mean).

## Why does this affect clothing?

The ministry believes holiness should be visible in everyday life, and that includes the way believers dress.

It does not treat clothing as the whole of holiness. Clothing is understood as part of a wider Christian manner of life that avoids worldly influence and keeps a clear distinction between the life of a believer and the culture around it.

## Why don't women wear trousers?

The passage most often cited is Deuteronomy 22:5:

> A woman must not wear men's clothing, nor a man wear women's clothing, for the LORD your God detests anyone who does this.
> — Deuteronomy 22:5, NIV

The ministry understands this as teaching that men and women should keep a clear distinction in their clothing, and applies it by encouraging women to wear dresses and skirts rather than trousers.

::note An application, not a quotation
:: The Bible does not mention modern trousers by name. In the world the verse was written for, men and women both wore robes, and trousers as we know them did not exist. So this is an application of the principle rather than a verse that says "women must not wear trousers" — which is why Christians who hold the same principle apply it in different ways. The practice as it is actually lived is described in [why women in the ministry dress that way](/articles/why-do-women-in-the-ministry-of-repentance-and-holiness-dress-that-way).

## Why are makeup and jewellery discouraged?

The ministry also places weight on modesty and simplicity.

Paul wrote:

> I also want the women to dress modestly, with decency and propriety, adorning themselves, not with elaborate hairstyles or gold or pearls or expensive clothes.
> — 1 Timothy 2:9, NIV

Peter wrote in the same direction:

> Your beauty should not come from outward adornment, such as elaborate hairstyles and the wearing of gold jewellery or fine clothes.
> — 1 Peter 3:3, NIV

The ministry reads these passages as turning believers away from an excessive attention to outward appearance and towards a life focused on God. That is why makeup and jewellery are discouraged. The emphasis is on **simplicity, modesty and inner holiness rather than outward display.**

## Is jewellery itself always sinful?

Here it is important to be honest about what the Bible does and does not say.

Scripture contains examples of jewellery that carry no rebuke at all. In Genesis 24, Rebekah is given a gold nose ring and bracelets. In Luke 15, the father of the returning son puts a ring on his hand — a sign of restoration, in a parable Jesus told about the mercy of God.

So Scripture does not say that every piece of jewellery is automatically sinful.

The Ministry of Repentance and Holiness takes a stricter position than that. It holds that avoiding jewellery and cosmetics is a clearer way of living out the biblical call to modesty, simplicity and separation from worldly values.

The distinction matters: **the ministry's standard is an application of its understanding of holiness, not a claim that Scripture contains a verse saying "jewellery is always a sin."**

## Is this what saves a person?

No. The foundation of salvation is Jesus Christ.

> For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith — and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God — not by works, so that no one can boast.
> — Ephesians 2:8–9, NIV

Wearing a dress, avoiding makeup or refusing jewellery cannot save anyone. The ministry's teaching is that outward changes should come from a life already changed through repentance and faith.

**The clothes are not the foundation of holiness. The changed heart is.**

## Holiness is bigger than clothing

This is perhaps the most important part to understand.

A person can dress modestly and still be proud, dishonest, jealous, unkind or full of hatred. That is not the holiness the Bible teaches.

Paul describes what a life led by the Spirit produces:

> The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, forbearance, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
> — Galatians 5:22–23, NIV

None of those can be measured by someone's clothes — and a standard that can be met by changing what you wear, while the list above goes unchanged, has measured the wrong thing.

So the teaching on trousers, makeup and jewellery makes most sense inside the larger message: **repentance leads to a changed life, a changed life should produce holiness, and holiness should affect the way a believer lives every day.**

The outward appearance is one part of that life. The greater question is what is happening in the heart. That whole argument is laid out in [what repentance and holiness are](/articles/what-is-repentance-and-holiness).

## So, why no trousers, makeup or jewellery?

The Ministry of Repentance and Holiness teaches these standards because it believes Christians are called to live differently from the world, and to show through their daily lives that they belong to God.

The message is not about clothing. It is about **repentance, holiness, righteousness and readiness for Christ's return**, and the clothing standards are one visible expression of that belief.

Whether a reader agrees with every application or not, the central question is the same: **is my life truly changing because I have chosen to follow Christ?**

Because biblical holiness is not about looking different. **It is about becoming different.**
